dedupe_keys.name: web decision support for road accessibility and emergency facility allocation during floods in cedar rapids and charles city iowa

description: This study presents a web application that shows how floods cut road access and helps decide where to place emergency facilities, tested in Cedar Rapids and Charles City, two flood-prone communities in Iowa. Yazeed Alabbad, Jerry Mount, Ann Melissa Campbell and İbrahim Demir of the University of Iowa and King Saud University published it in Urban Informatics in 2024. The framework uses graph network methods and current web standards to translate flood events into operational constraints on the road network, and lets non-expert users see road and bridge status, shortest paths to critical amenities, arbitrary point-to-point routes, location-allocation of emergency facilities and service coverage. The tests show that flooding significantly affects bridge operation, routing to critical amenities, facility placement and service area accessibility. Coverage: two Iowa communities under flood scenarios. Access: open-access article; the public address of the application was not confirmed. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: deterministic flood scenarios, no traffic congestion or dynamic demand, and results tied to the two test sites. It supports emergency response planning, network flow and hazard exposure analysis of road networks in floods. Similar analyses can be built with the OSMnx and openrouteservice tools in the catalogue.
